candidates.rationale: A donates TS_STD($volume,21) (3 nodes, volume-instability level); B donates ($close - $low) (3 nodes, close's distance above the low). Rather than reuse either parent's own normalizer, B's numerator is rescaled by A's volume-dispersion measure instead of a price-based denominator -- a liquidity-conditioned recovery-off-the-low signal -- then crossed with a fresh earnings rank. Neither parent alone states this: A never sees price positioning or a fundamental, B never sees volume. The close-low fragment also appears in unrelated live siblings (e.g. c0a5abed0f7ea0f7's close-low/TS_STD($close,21) form); the denominator field (volume vs close) should keep correlation under 0.80 but that is not numerically verified.

Both parents are RANK($eps) - RANK(X) instances of an already-saturated template (9+ live siblings), so the fusion deliberately drops that shared shape instead of adding a tenth. A donates ($close - $low) (3 nodes); B donates TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes, kept under ABS so it isn't RANKed directly and doesn't recreate B's own RANK(TS_DELTA($volume,3))). The two are multiplied into one joint quantity and TS_RANKed within each stock's own 21-day history, flagging a recovery only when it coincides with an unusual volume change in either direction -- a confirmation interaction neither parent states -- while TS_RANK keeps the joint statistic comparable across stocks of different price and volume scale.

A donates TS_MAX($dollar_volume,21) (3 nodes, 21-day peak liquidity); B donates TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes, divided rather than RANKed so it doesn't recreate B's own RANK(TS_DELTA($volume,3))). B's short-horizon share-volume delta is rescaled by A's own recent dollar-liquidity ceiling, so a given volume change reads as a bigger surprise in a name whose typical liquidity is low than in a heavily-traded mega-cap; crossed with a fresh earnings rank. Neither parent normalizes a volume change by the stock's own liquidity scale. The share/dollar-volume unit mix is a deliberate scale adjustment (this codebase already mixes such units elsewhere, e.g. dcc42219621b8def), but correlation with sibling accrual_gap x volume-delta factors (98f5e83e9268cb7d and family) is unverified.

A donates TS_DELTA($volume,3) (3 nodes, under ABS so it doesn't recreate A's own RANK(TS_DELTA($volume,3))); B donates TS_MIN($low,21) (3 nodes, the 21-day floor). The floor is paired with the day's high rather than close to avoid restating B's own 5-node close-to-floor numerator, then TS_RANKed within the stock's own 63-day history (avoiding a cross-sectional raw-price-level scale mismatch) to measure how far today's high reaches above the recent floor; crossed with A's unsigned volume-shock magnitude. This asks whether a reach above the recent floor is volume-confirmed, which neither parent expresses alone: A never touches the price range, B has no volume or fundamental input.

A donates TS_MIN($low,21) (3 nodes, the 21-day price floor); B donates ($book_per_share + 1e-8) (3 nodes, its only legal fragment beyond the 2-node ABS(eps) leaf). The floor price is normalized by book value per share instead of B's own earnings numerator, producing a trough price-to-book ratio -- a margin-of-safety measure using the stock's recent low rather than its current price. Neither parent states this: A is a pure price oscillator with no fundamental, B never references price history.

Same parent pair as the prior cross, fused on the opposite extremum and as a distance rather than a level: A donates TS_MAX($high,21) (3 nodes, the 21-day ceiling) instead of the floor; B again donates ($book_per_share + 1e-8) (3 nodes). Close is compared against its own recent high (typically <= 0) and the drawdown is scaled by book value per share -- a capitulation/de-rating-severity measure in book-value units, the opposite-in-spirit construction to the trough-price-to-book ratio. Both crosses share the same book_per_share guard, so some positive correlation between the two is plausible, though a level ratio and a drawdown-from-peak ratio should behave differently in practice; unverified.

A donates TS_MAX($high,21) (3 nodes, the 21-day ceiling); B donates TS_DELTA($book_per_share,63) (3 nodes, divided rather than RANKed so it doesn't recreate B's own RANK(TS_DELTA($book_per_share,63))). Quarterly per-share book-value growth is scaled by the stock's own recent price ceiling, asking how much fundamental value grew relative to what the market recently paid at the peak; crossed with B's own accrual_gap rank as an independent accounting-quality gate. Neither parent normalizes a fundamental change by a price extremum, and A never sees a fundamental at all.

A donates TS_DELTA($book_per_share,63) (3 nodes, divided by the current book-value level rather than RANKed directly -- turning a raw dollar delta into a per-share growth rate and avoiding A's own RANK(TS_DELTA($book_per_share,63))); B donates TS_MAX($dollar_volume,21) (3 nodes, the same peak-liquidity leg used in the eps/dollar-volume cross, here TS_RANKed against the stock's own 63-day liquidity history instead of reused inside B's price-scaled ratio). This asks whether proportional book-value growth coincides with an elevated liquidity regime for that name -- a growth-meets-attention interaction. A has no liquidity input at all, and B never scales its liquidity peak by anything but price.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
